overlay.basis: Read by a person from aagento-bridge rcc-slab-2-rule-engine.ts. This file is byte-identical (besides the class name) to arch-bridge-rule-engine.ts, so the railway RCC slab/arch family shares the railway arch bridge's own geometry: an RCC box with an arch-shaped masonry fill above it, coped. Every geometry value is added to levels in metres (z_bot = bedLvl - wearC - tSB, line 38-39), so parameters and outputs are metres unless noted.

findings.text: rcc-slab-2-rule-engine.ts is byte-identical to arch-bridge-rule-engine.ts apart from the class name (RccSlab2RuleEngine vs ArchBridgeRuleEngine): rcc_slab and railway_arch_bridge are the same rule engine registered under two family keys.
compute() reads fields the family defaults do not hold; the code then uses its own constants: geometry.height_above_masonry → None, options2d.show_return_wall → None

wearing course on the bottom slab (bed level is its top)

embankment side slope, horizontal per vertical

PCC sub-base thickness under the bottom slab

bed level: the finished floor, top of the wearing course
wing walls are part of the arrangement
curtain wall is part of the arrangement
height above the arch masonry as entered (else derived from formation level)
return wall is part of the arrangement
